design.objective: Place the desktop sidebar-collapse control before the project selector and render route tabs in a separate full-width row below the global header while preserving mobile and tab behavior.
users: Desktop users controlling the sidebar, project context and route tabs
Phone users retaining the already accepted compact header and sticky tabs

requirements.statement: Desktop renders the sidebar-collapse control immediately before the project selector in the global header.
acceptance: The collapse control is visually left of the project selector
Both controls remain clickable and do not overlap
requirements.source: User screenshot annotation and confirmed option A
counterexample: The project selector appears before the collapse control

requirements.statement: Desktop renders UiTabs as a separate full-width row directly below the global header and does not render a breadcrumb.
acceptance: UiTabs is not a descendant of app-header
The tab row spans the content width below the header
No breadcrumb is visible on desktop
requirements.source: User screenshot annotation and confirmed option A
counterexample: Tabs remain between the project selector and global actions

requirements.statement: Existing route-tab navigation and context-menu commands retain their behavior.
acceptance: Switch, close, refresh, close others and close all keep their current semantics
requirements.source: Existing UiTabs contract and prior acceptance
counterexample: Moving the tab row resets tabsStore or changes closability

requirements.statement: Phone viewports retain the current compact header, current-page title, sticky separate tab row and project selector in the navigation drawer.
acceptance: 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 remain usable without horizontal overflow
requirements.source: Prior accepted mobile behavior and confirmed scope
counterexample: The mobile title is compressed or the project selector disappears

requirements.statement: Global header controls and the independent tab row remain geometrically stable across supported desktop layouts.
acceptance: Multiple tabs do not displace header controls
The document has no page-level horizontal overflow
counterexample: Opening tabs pushes the account control outside the viewport

invariants: tabsStore remains the sole route-tab state source
UiTabs remains responsible for tab commands and context menu
Project context, sidebar collapse and global account actions remain usable
No page-level horizontal overflow is introduced
constraints: Use existing Vue 3, Element Plus and shell components
Do not add dependencies or modify backend and business pages
Limit product edits to AppLayout.vue and styles.css
Preserve the current 760px mobile breakpoint behavior
non_goals: Changing route-tab persistence, caching or command semantics
Redesigning sidebar menus, top-navigation mode or business pages

selected_approach.name: Separate global header and route-tab row
selected_approach.reason: It exactly matches the confirmed visual hierarchy and removes width competition between route tabs and global controls.

alternatives.name: Two rows inside app-header
alternatives.rejected_because: It couples header height, sticky behavior and tab layout in one container.

alternatives.name: Keep inline tabs and only reorder collapse/project controls
alternatives.rejected_because: It does not satisfy the requested independent tab row.

components.name: AppLayout
components.responsibility: Order collapse and project controls in the header and mount UiTabs below it

components.name: UiTabs
components.responsibility: Render and operate route tabs without layout awareness

components.name: shell styles
components.responsibility: Keep the header controls stable and render a full-width independent tab row

interfaces.name: UiTabs currentPath prop
interfaces.contract: currentPath remains route.fullPath after the mount move

interfaces.name: sidebar collapse action
interfaces.contract: The action continues to toggle theme.sidebarCollapsed

data_flows.input: collapse click, project selection, route.fullPath and tabsStore.tabs
data_flows.output: two-level desktop shell with unchanged behavior

error_handling.condition: Tab count exceeds the row width
error_handling.behavior: Element Plus tab navigation handles horizontal overflow inside the independent row
error_handling.recovery: Close tabs or use tab navigation controls

error_handling.behavior: Existing compact header and sticky tab rules remain active

performance: No additional requests or duplicated tab state
compatibility: Preserve tab commands, layout modes and required phone viewports
operations: Build, DOM ordering, geometry, interaction and console checks provide evidence

verification_strategy.signal: Desktop control order and two-row geometry match the confirmed design
verification_strategy.method: Browser DOM and rectangle checks with multiple tabs

verification_strategy.signal: All tab commands retain existing outcomes
verification_strategy.method: Switch, close, refresh and context-menu browser interactions

verification_strategy.signal: Mobile retains title, sticky tabs, project entry and no overflow
No type, build or whitespace regression
verification_strategy.method: npm --prefix web run build and focused git diff --check

assumptions.text: The existing standalone .ui-tabs-bar styling remains suitable after restoring the desktop mount below app-header
assumptions.basis: The application used this structure before the inline-header revision
assumptions.falsifier: Browser geometry shows unexpected width, border or sticky behavior

decisions.decision: Place the desktop collapse control before the project selector
decisions.reason: Matches the user's marked control order

decisions.decision: Render desktop tabs in a separate row below the header without restoring breadcrumbs
decisions.reason: Matches the requested hierarchy while avoiding duplicate page titles
The request only revises desktop placement and the current mobile layout has passed acceptance

risks.risk: The independent row restores about 44px of shell height
risks.mitigation: This is the explicitly selected visual hierarchy; keep the row compact

risks.risk: Top and mixed layouts differ in available collapse/project controls
risks.impact: Incorrect ordering or empty space in one layout mode
risks.mitigation: Verify each supported desktop layout mode before completion

approval.evidence: User reviewed the landed option-A design and explicitly directed implementation.

global_constraints: Only modify web/src/views/AppLayout.vue and web/src/styles.css product surfaces
Do not change UiTabs, tabsStore, routes, business pages, backend or dependencies
Do not restore the desktop breadcrumb
Preserve the current mobile title, sticky tabs and drawer project selector
Preserve unrelated dirty-worktree changes and do not commit or push

file_map.responsibility: Compose collapse, project, global actions and the single UiTabs mount
file_map.evidence: Current template owns all shell mount positions

file_map.responsibility: Define header order, standalone tab row, responsive stickiness and overflow
file_map.evidence: Current selectors own app-header, ui-tabs-bar and 760px behavior

tasks.goal: Place the desktop collapse control before project selection and restore a separate route-tab row without changing tab or mobile behavior.

Desktop UiTabs is currently mounted inside .app-header__tabs

steps.evidence: Focused template diff and DOM count

steps.action: Remove inline-tab CSS and retain stable standalone tab/header responsive styles

steps.action: Verify side, top and mixed desktop layouts plus all tab commands
steps.expected: No empty header, overlap or behavior regression
steps.evidence: DOM, rectangles, interactions and width measurements

steps.action: Verify 375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 plus a fresh console sample
steps.expected: One sticky tab row, readable title, usable drawer project selector, no overflow or new console errors
steps.evidence: Mobile DOM, geometry and console records

acceptance_checks: Desktop collapse control is left of project selection wherever a side navigation exists
Desktop UiTabs is a separate full-width row and no breadcrumb is visible

Top and mixed layouts do not contain an empty second header
375x812, 390x844 and 430x932 retain current mobile behavior without horizontal overflow
Frontend build, focused diff and fresh console checks pass
risks: Top or mixed layout may retain an empty app-header

tasks.rollback: Restore the pre-task AppLayout control order, UiTabs mount conditions and corresponding shell CSS while preserving unrelated file changes.
stop_conditions: The change requires UiTabs, tabsStore, route, business-page or backend edits
A layout mode requires a new product decision
Mobile regression cannot be fixed within the two approved files
escalation_conditions: The breadcrumb or mobile design must change
A supported layout mode must be removed or project context relocated
